b: A ten-year-old works her way out of a bathhouse for spirits and back to her own name.
Two sisters, a mother in hospital, and the forest spirit who waits with them at a bus stop in the rain.
A young witch moves to the city alone and learns that a gift can leave you, and come back.
A mining-town boy, a girl who falls from the sky, and a floating city everyone wants to own.

t: Nausicaä of the Valley of the Wind
b: A princess who listens to the giant insects everyone else wants to burn.
Forest gods against an ironworks town, and nobody in it is simply the villain.
A brother and sister alone in the last months of the war. Watch it when you are ready for it.

t: The Tale of the Princess Kaguya
b: Takahata's last film: the oldest Japanese folk tale, drawn in charcoal and watercolour.

ph: 君たちはどう生きるか
b: A grieving boy follows a heron into another world, in the film Miyazaki titled How Do You Live?
Biker gangs, a psychic catastrophe and the most ambitious hand-drawn city ever put on film.
A cyborg agent wonders how much of her is really her.
A girl guards an egg in a drowned city. Almost wordless, and unlike anything else.
A pop idol becomes an actress and loses track of which life is hers.
An old film star tells her life story, and the interviewers fall into it.

ph: 東京ゴッドファーザーズ
b: Three homeless Tokyoites find a baby on Christmas Eve.
A device lets therapists walk into patients' dreams. Then someone steals it.
Lupin the Third, a counterfeiting count, and Miyazaki's first feature.

ph: 愛・おぼえていますか
b: A war against giants who have never heard a love song.

t: The Girl Who Leapt Through Time
b: A schoolgirl learns to jump back in time and spends it on karaoke, until it matters.
Three chapters of one long longing, measured in train journeys and falling blossoms.

ph: おおかみこどもの雨と雪
b: A widowed student raises two children who are half wolf.
A city boy and a country girl swap bodies. Then the story turns.
A former bully tries to make amends with the deaf girl he tormented.

t: In This Corner of the World
b: Daily life in Kure, near Hiroshima, 1944–45, through a young wife who loves to draw.
Two girls who draw manga, and the hour of film about why anyone keeps drawing.
The war story that made giant robots into weapons and their pilots into frightened teenagers.
Bread, cheese, goats and weather: the drama of an ordinary life.
A clumsy schoolgirl, her friends, and the transformation sequence a generation memorised.
A boy who cannot make himself climb into the robot. Then the show turns inward.
A girl who wants to be a prince, duels for a bride, and takes the fairy tale apart.
Bounty hunters drift through space to a jazz score, each running from a past.
A quiet girl, a new computer, and a network that may be talking back.
A wanderer cures the ailments caused by life forms older than plants and animals.
Two brothers pay for one forbidden act with their bodies and spend years paying it back.
A magical-girl story that asks what the wish really costs.
Humanity behind walls, giants outside. Then the walls come down, and so does the story's idea of who the enemy is.
Table tennis as a study of talent and what it does to friends. Drawn by Masaaki Yuasa in a rough, joyful line.
A psychic boy who would rather be ordinary, and a con-man mentor who turns out to be decent.
A former child soldier writes other people's letters, trying to learn what “I love you” means.
A boy hunts demons to save his sister, and grieves for every demon he kills.
A guitarist so anxious she can barely speak joins a band. Very funny, and very kind.
The heroes have already won. The elf who will outlive them all starts to learn what the journey meant.
